{"self_assessment": "Impact: I proposed the fish in the first seconds and sketched it on the pad, with the top line and belly both leaving from the nose so one push could run through everything. The fish is big and fills most of the table, so the outline reads clearly. I laid the start domino and most of stroke 1, the long top line and the tail sweep, which is the longest single run in the picture. Before the push, my by-eye trace showed 109 of the 110 standing dominoes connected to the start.

Execution: I redrew the tail as one wide rounded sweep with no notch and no pointy tips, which suits how dominoes pass the fall. I carried stroke 1 on from the line near the dip round to the belly end, making sure the sweep met the belly side-on and not head-on. I then inspected that join closely and closed up the tail. I left the one stray alone rather than risk the top line, and I called for hands off before the push.

Collaboration: I split the work in the first minute: Omar took the belly, Hana and Jack took checks and fixes, and I took the start and the top line. I took Hana's feedback on the tail and acted on it. I asked Jack to hold off on the belly join so we didn't double up. I kept the table informed about what I was laying and where.

Leadership: I set the direction early, picked an animal whose outline reads from the fallen dominoes alone, and kept the team to a simple plan. I kept the table calm and organized through the hand-off from building to hands-off waiting. I believe I drove about 40% of the table's result, since the design and most of the longest run were mine, and the belly, the checks and the cleanup from the others were also needed.", "my_share_percent": 40}
